title: NYSERDA awards eight bulk energy storage projects and 13 large-scale renewable projects (press release)
key_claim: NYSERDA contracted eight bulk storage projects totalling 950 MW from 46 bids of about 6 GW; payments start only after commercial operation and all required permits and local approvals; projects must meet the storage safety codes effective January 2026 and be in service by the end of 2030; a second solicitation follows by year-end toward 3 GW over three solicitations.
frame_summary: The state agency presents the awards as progress toward its storage target and answers fire-safety concerns through contract terms, while paying only for projects that have secured every permit and local approval.
verbatim_quote: Payments under these contracts will not commence until projects have begun commercial operation, after having obtained all required permits and local approvals.
verbatim_list: Once operational, the eight contracted bulk energy storage projects will add 950 megawatts (MW) of new energy storage capacity.
They were selected through a competitive process that included bid proposals from 46 projects totaling approximately 6 GW of capacity.
are contractually required to meet the new storage safety codes that became effective January 1, 2026
All projects are expected to be placed in-service by the end of 2030
to continue progress toward procuring 3 GW of bulk energy storage over three solicitations

title: 2026 Reliability Needs Assessment: preliminary base case results (ESPWG/TPAS, 23 July 2026)
key_claim: The 2026 RNA preliminary base case finds New York City deficient by about 130 MW in 2031 growing to over 1,800 MW in 2036, with a statewide deficiency of approximately 200 MW from 2033, and its Key Assumptions list about 6,200 MW of proposed solar, wind and storage projects.
frame_summary: The grid operator argues that reliability needs emerge from the early 2030s because retirements outpace the supply additions its base case assumes, so new resources have to arrive.
verbatim_quote: NYC is deficient about 130 MW (2031) growing to over 1,800 MW (2036)
verbatim_list: ~6,200 MW of solar, wind, and storage proposed projects
The base case exceeds the state's resource adequacy criterion starting in 2033 with a deficiency of approximately 200 MW
notes: Primary system-operator planning presentation. The 6,200 MW line sits under the 'Key Assumptions' heading (Generation). Fetched live 06/10/2026; title-page date 'July 23, 2026, KCC'.

title: Resolution 168-26 extending the battery energy storage moratorium (Town Board, Westchester County)
date_evidence: Adopted on July 21, 2026 At a Regular Meeting Held at Town Hall
key_claim: The Cortlandt Town Board extended its moratorium on new commercial battery energy storage applications through December 31, 2026, first enacted in 2024 and extended three times since, citing its own committee's draft law and the prudence of waiting for State guidance.
frame_summary: The town board argues that a pause on battery applications should continue while its own local law is finished and the State issues more guidance.
verbatim_quote: The moratorium herein shall be extended through December 31, 2026 unless terminated earlier.
verbatim_list: The Town originally enacted a moratorium pursuant to Local Law Number 2-2024.
The Town Board believes it to be prudent to allow the State to issue additional guidance.
notes: Primary municipal record. The resolution lists Local Laws 10-2024, 2-2025 and 7-2025 as earlier extensions. Fetched live 06/10/2026; on-page text for verbatim_quote re-checked by WebFetch (device audit blocked: 403 via proxy).

title: NYSERDA Index Storage Credit solicitation: Round 1 winners
key_claim: NYISO Zones J and K took 54% of awarded capacity; Zones D, E, F and H received no awards from 14 bids; Zenobe Burns has held town permits since early 2026, Holtsville had a required county variance denied and is in court, and KCE NY 5 has no local approvals yet.
frame_summary: The market analyst argues the first awards favour downstate sites and lithium, and that delivery risk differs sharply across winners because some still lack local approvals or interconnection.
verbatim_quote: NYISO Zones J and K took 54% of the awarded capacity.
verbatim_list: Zones D, E, F, and H received no awards. Their 14 bids included six of the seven non-lithium projects.
Zenobē Burns has held town permits since early 2026.
Holtsville targets December 2028, the earliest date. However, Suffolk County's health department denied it a required variance, and Savion is challenging that decision in court.
KCE NY 5, by contrast, has no local approvals yet. It sits on county-owned land in New Paltz, and in September 2026 Ulster County's legislature delayed a vote on leading its environmental review.

title: Opposition to Renewable Energy Facilities in the United States: September 2026 Edition
key_claim: By the end of 2025 at least 888 state and local restrictions blocking renewable projects had been adopted and at least 567 projects faced significant local opposition across 48 states; the report covers siting of solar, wind, battery storage and related transmission.
frame_summary: The Columbia researchers argue that state and local restrictions and project-level opposition are a widespread and growing barrier to renewable energy siting across the United States.
verbatim_quote: at least 888 state and local restrictions blocking renewable energy projects had been adopted and that there were at least 567 projects that faced significant local opposition, across 48 states, by the end of 2025.
notes: Counts cover all renewable technologies, not storage alone; the body says so. Fetched live 06/10/2026 (report page and the 03/09/2026 Sabin blog post).

title: Town in Adirondacks adopts moratorium on battery storage permits with no project proposed (Newcomb, NY)
key_claim: Newcomb, New York adopted a 12-month battery storage moratorium on 14 July before any proposal had been submitted, joining Ticonderoga, Jay and St. Armand.
frame_summary: The article presents a small town pausing battery permits pre-emptively, to study fire risk and write local law before any project arrives.
verbatim_quote: Town officials said no BESS proposal has been submitted in Newcomb, but they wanted to have a policy in place before any project is proposed.
verbatim_list: Newcomb now joins Essex County communities including Ticonderoga, Jay, and St. Armand that have acted to prohibit BESS.
notes: Tier 3 secondary, used only to corroborate that some moratoria pre-date any project. Fetched live 06/10/2026; on-page text for verbatim_quote re-checked by WebFetch (device audit blocked: 403 via proxy).
